summary: Inventory of what a Swift port (iOS one sandboxed process, macOS) needs from the MIMo body under D:/UEMA_Research/third_party/MIMo. The body is MuJoCo XML (v2 body: 75 geoms, all primitives, 0 mesh files; 97 joints; 92 motor actuators; 54 torque sensors + 1 accelerometer + 1 gyro; 93 joint equality locks; 6 patched finger tendons), and the bridge's three named scenes (reach, selfbody, floor) are generated wrappers around MIMo_metav2.xml (41,064 bytes) and MIMo_modelv2.xml (38,486 bytes) with primitive-geom props; with the default lite textures no MIMo PNG is loaded, and the floor pattern is a 1024x1024 PNG generated at run time. Per model step (50 ms = action_repeat 5 x env step 10 ms = 10 physics steps of 5 ms): physics, contact forces, torque/accelerometer/gyro sensor values, joint angles and body poses are all MuJoCo C calls (portable). Vestibular and proprioception are direct array reads (38 and 110 Python lines; the bridge reads the arrays itself). Motor/actuation on the bridge path is SpringDamperModel: clip + write data.ctrl (91-line class; the real per-step work is 2 lines); the bridge's own command decoding (action_decoder.py, 527 lines) is outside MIMo. Tactile is the heavy Python: TrimeshTouch runs a Python loop over data.ncon with mj_contactForce (C) and then numpy/trimesh/networkx distance-and-BFS searches with an LRU cache (895 lines without plotting, plus 18 scale_linear, 33 _contains, 82 base class; setup helpers sensorpoints.py 426, sensormeshes.py 316 with scipy Delaunay, cache.py 54; utils.py frame math 680 non-plot lines), and the bridge swaps in its own response function (contact_mechanics.py lines 60-76) and fixed inside-test directions (touch_inside_rays.py). Vision: MIMo's SimpleVision (234 lines, numpy FFT acuity, cv2 foveation) is not used by the bridge; the bridge renders eye cameras with MuJoCo's OpenGL mjr_render on a mujoco.GLContext (env.py 603-638), eye 256 px default, fovea 288 px at 24 deg, ring 150 deg in the released run, which is the iOS rendering blocker. No audio or intermind module exists in MIMo. The released weights' args.json names scene 'crib' (mobile, critters, responsive caregiver, age fixed:24, trunk_v1), not reach/selfbody/floor; growth to age 24 is XML preprocessing (2,601 Python lines) that can run once on a desktop.

summary: Two input paths exist and only one of them is what D:/UEMA_Research/Source/Python/mimo_bridge/lem_model.py consumes. (1) The UE / Mode-B path: tokenizer/tokenizer.py LEMTokenizer reads one 31,040-byte frame from Windows named shared memory (transport/cpu_reader.py: mmap with a tagname) and vision from D3D12-to-CUDA textures (transport/gpu_reader.py: `import cuda_d3d12_interop`); the per-sense functions in tokenizer/modalities/*.py then parse the bytes with struct.unpack_from and numpy on the CPU and return CPU float32 tensors; vision patches are cut on the graphics card by a JIT CUDA kernel (modalities/vision_kernels.py, needs nvcc + MSVC, falls back to plain torch index/reshape ops when it cannot compile). (2) The MIMo bridge path: mimo_bridge/datasource.py packs the same 31,040-byte frame in-process (frame_encoder.encode_frame) and decodes it with the same tokenize_* functions on device "cpu" (frame_encoder.decode_with_model_tokenizer); vision patches come from mimo_bridge/vision_adapter.py (numpy, CPU: (N,768) float32 patches + (N,4) float32 angles); vestibular comes from mimo_bridge/vestibular_adapter.py (29 float32 numbers per frame) normalised by numpy float64 running statistics to [B,28] float32 in vestibular_sense.py; intermind is a synthetic placeholder ([n_agents, d_model+3]) or is replaced by the vestibular sense under --vestibular-sense. Per sense, the token arrays are: vision [32506,16,16,3] float32 (UE) or [N,768] float32 + [N,4] (bridge); tactile (code name `touch`) [256,10] float32 patches + [16,8] collisions from the tokenizer, turned into a [32,19] per-body point cloud in lem_model.touch_point_cloud; audio [256,2] + [5] float32 read from a spectrum computed elsewhere (UE C++ FFT or audio_adapter numpy), no FFT inside the tokenizer; proprioception [n<=24,12] float32 (bridge extends to 26 rows under trunk_v1); motor [24,10] float32 (bridge 26 rows; lem_model widens each row with 9 zero command columns to 19); vestibular [B,28] float32; intermind torch.zeros(3) stub. All tokenizer computation is CPU numpy/struct except the vision patch cut and the LUT/id tensors that VisionTokenizer allocates on config.device. float64 appears in numpy on the bridge side only (touch_adapter Goertzel loop, vestibular statistics, vision_adapter rays, audio_adapter spectra), all cast to float32 before torch, plus a few torch float64 tensors in lem_model (hand joint angles, lines 2533-2534) and lem/model modules; scipy is imported only inside functions of mimo_bridge/hand_target_control.py and limb_target_control.py and in audio_adapter.render_track (video soundtrack) and offline tools; a grep over tokenizer, lem and mimo_bridge (tests excluded) finds no `import cv2`. lem_model.py imports two functions from lem/live_test.py: apply_developmental_constraints (clone, clamp, multiply, torch.tensor on motor_out.device) and _run_imagination_compiled (torch + lem.model.predictive_state.transition, F.mse_loss); neither calls CUDA or anything from the Unreal pipeline; importing lem.live_test does import the tokenizer package (torch, numpy, mmap module) and runs logging.basicConfig at import, and its CUDA use sits inside main(). lem_model.py does not import lem/native_ops.py (that extension, which includes cuda.h and loads a second NVRTC patchify kernel, is imported by lem/replay_buffer.py and lem/training_step.py); lem_model uses mimo_bridge/replay.py and falls back to CPU when torch.cuda.is_available() is False.

findings.topic: vision (UE): JIT CUDA kernel needs nvcc and MSVC
findings.meaning_for_port: The kernel (line 102 `__global__ void bgra_to_rgb_patches_kernel(`) is CUDA C compiled at run time with `extra_cuda_cflags=['-allow-unsupported-compiler']` (line 236). It cannot build on Apple hardware; the loader catches every exception and returns None (line 269 `log.warning("CUDA vision kernels unavailable (nvcc not found?): %s", e)`), so vision.py uses its torch fallback. The module is dead weight on Apple, not a crash.

`where` is a Windows command; line 202 hard-codes `cuda_default = r'C:\Program Files\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\CUDA'`. Both sit inside the try/except of load_vision_kernels (lines 199-270), so on Apple hardware they fail and the fallback path is taken. Whether a Python without the subprocess module raises something the except catches is an open question.

summary: Inventory of D:/UEMA_Research dashboard, explainer and movement viewer for a port. SERVER: the dashboard is Python's standard library http.server (ThreadingHTTPServer bound to 127.0.0.1, default port 8766); no web framework. The explainer is a builder script that writes one self-contained HTML page (Saved/mimo_bridge/explainer.html) from a run folder's args.json, model_receipt.json, replay_training_stats.jsonl, explain/step_N.json snapshots, checkpoints' model.safetensors (read with safetensors, framework="np") and docs/gain_of_function_v4 json files; its page uses inlined viewer.js (canvas heatmaps, hand-rolled SVG, base64 PNG eye images). The movement viewer is a package (sources/commands/index/render/probes/auto/service/api) plus movement_viewer.js; the dashboard answers /api/movement/* from its index files and serves PNGs from a pictures folder; a separate service process draws the pictures. PICTURES: MuJoCo's own offscreen renderer (mujoco.Renderer, mujoco==3.3.0) after forward kinematics (mj_kinematics, mj_comPos) on the recording's saved compiled model (.mjb.gz, loaded with MjModel.from_binary_path); pixels saved with Pillow; no matplotlib in the viewer (matplotlib Agg is used only by the trainer-side snapshot capture for eye PNGs). GL backend: nothing sets MUJOCO_GL for the viewer; mujoco's gl_context picks WGL via GLFW on Windows and CGL on Darwin, so macOS needs no code change for offscreen drawing; the live 3D window (mujoco.viewer.launch_passive) refuses on macOS unless run under mjpython. WINDOWS-ONLY CODE: all guarded (os.name == "nt" for msvcrt/fcntl locks, psutil priority, kernel32 power-throttling opt-out, DETACHED_PROCESS/CREATE_NO_WINDOW via getattr fallbacks) except: commit_guard's HEAVY_LOCK hard-codes C:/Users/bhart/...; commit_guard returns "allowed" off Windows (no memory guard); the dashboard prints a PowerShell copy-paste command and prefers .venv_mimo\Scripts\python.exe (falls back to sys.executable); "PDT"/"PST" labels are hard-coded in the export page; drive-letter roots (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/..., D:/UEMA_archive/...) are re-rooted by repo_paths.localize for the recorded roots only, and D:/UEMA_archive is not a recorded root. NOT NEEDED TO RUN THE MODEL: the trainer imports the explainer's capture/writer only when --explain-* flags are set, and imports nothing from the dashboard or movement viewer; the viewer deliberately avoids importing torch. DATA FOR A SWIFT VIEW: bars come from Saved/mimo_bridge/movement_viewer/index/<rec>/b<body>.npz (+ .json meta); each drawing is a folder <pictures>/<20-hex key>/ with 9 (lite) or more PNGs named hand_<left|right>_<front|side>_<state>.png and body_<front|left|right>_<state>.png plus manifest.json holding every handle's target (cm, quaternion xyzw) and per-sample errors, every finger joint's angle (start, target, samples, after_next), measures, contacts, posture; drawing new pictures needs the chunk files (npz: delta-coded qpos with quanta 1e-6/1e-7, order_motor [k,26,9], order_mask [k,26], order_hand_goal [k,44]) plus the MuJoCo model for forward kinematics, which no Swift code in the repository replaces. The release ships 6 indexed recordings whose chunk paths point at D:/UEMA_archive (absent) and 206 drawn manifests, so bars and existing pictures display anywhere; new drawings need recordings under a ROOTS pattern.
